posts.big_note: Americans' projected online Black Friday spending — a record, up 9.2% — while Canadians rein it in
posts.headline: Americans just set a Black Friday record online — a projected $12.9 billion, up 9.2% — while Canadians put 62 cents of every dollar toward essentials.
posts.source: Source: Adobe Analytics (U.S.) & BCG 2026 study (Canada), Nov. 2026
posts.caption:
Same weekend, two different economies.

In the U.S., Adobe Analytics projects a record $12.9 billion spent online on Black Friday — up about 9.2% from last year's $11.8 billion. That's the sixth straight record, after $10.8 billion in 2024.

Across the border, the mood is colder. In BCG's 2026 year-end study, Canadians say 62 cents of every Black Friday dollar is going to essentials, not gifts — and nearly nine in ten say they're worried about food and energy costs.

My take: a "record" headline hides who's actually spending. More dollars can just mean steeper prices and more borrowing, not more under the tree. The Canadian number is the honest one — people buying what they need, skipping what they don't.

Which camp are you in this year — splurging, or sticking to essentials? 👇

Source: Adobe Analytics and BCG 2026 Year-End Sales Events Consumer Study (Nov. 2026)

#BlackFriday #Holiday #PersonalFinance #FollowTheMoney

paragraphs: In the U.S., Adobe Analytics projects a record $12.9 billion spent online on Black Friday 2026 — up about 9.2% from last year's $11.8 billion record, and the sixth straight record after $10.8 billion in 2024.

In Canada, BCG's 2026 year-end consumer study found shoppers putting 62 cents of every Black Friday dollar toward essentials rather than gifts, with nearly nine in ten worried about food and energy costs.
The headline is a record. The quieter story is who is actually spending — and how much of it is need, not want, on both sides of the border.
